title: What Causes Crawl Space Mold?
h1: What Causes Crawl Space Mold, and How Do You Stop It?
description: Crawl space mold comes from moisture: damp soil, plumbing leaks, poor drainage and sweating ducts. Learn the causes and how to keep a crawl space dry.
quick_answer: Crawl space mold is caused by moisture. The usual sources are damp soil with no vapor barrier, rainwater that drains toward the foundation, plumbing leaks, sweating ducts and pipes, blocked vents, and dryer or bath fans that exhaust into the crawl space. Wood framing and dust supply the food, so controlling moisture is the way to prevent it.
body:
Why do crawl spaces get moldy?

Mold needs moisture, food and mild temperatures. A crawl space has the food in its wood joists, subfloor and any debris down there. It's usually dark and sheltered. So when moisture shows up and stays, mold follows.

Many San Diego County homes are built on slabs, but plenty of older homes and hillside homes sit on raised foundations with a crawl space underneath. Those spaces can stay damp much longer than you'd expect in a dry climate.

What are the most common causes?

  1. Damp soil. Bare dirt gives off moisture constantly. Without a vapor barrier, that moisture rises into the crawl space air and the wood above it.
  2. Poor drainage. Gutters that dump at the foundation, downspouts without extensions and soil that slopes toward the house all send rainwater under the home.
  3. Plumbing leaks. Slow drips from supply lines, drain pipes or the water heater can go unnoticed for months.
  4. Sweating ducts and pipes. Cold AC ducts or cold water lines can collect condensation when humid air hits them, especially if duct insulation is torn.
  5. Exhaust venting. Dryer vents and bath fans should never end in a crawl space. They dump warm, wet air right where you don't want it.
  6. Blocked foundation vents. Vents covered by plants, soil or storage stop air from carrying moisture out.
  7. Coastal humidity. In homes near the ocean, damp marine air flows in through vents and can condense on cooler surfaces underneath.

What are the signs of crawl space mold?

  • A musty, earthy smell in the house, often stronger in rooms over the crawl space
  • Fuzzy white, gray, green or black growth on joists or the subfloor
  • Damp or sagging insulation between floor joists
  • Standing water or wet soil after rain
  • Rusty nails, metal straps or ductwork
  • Soft spots or cupping in the floor above

Air from the crawl space moves up into the house through gaps around pipes, wiring and ducts, so a crawl space problem can affect indoor air quality upstairs too.

How do you prevent crawl space mold?

  • Fix drainage first. Clean gutters, extend downspouts away from the house and regrade soil so it slopes away from the foundation.
  • Repair leaks. Check plumbing and the water heater area for drips.
  • Lay a vapor barrier. A heavy plastic ground cover keeps soil moisture out of the air.
  • Route exhaust outdoors. Make sure dryer and bath fan ducts run all the way outside.
  • Keep vents clear, or, if the crawl space is being sealed, follow a proper encapsulation plan with moisture control.
  • Seal and insulate ducts. Leaky or uninsulated ducts in a crawl space add moisture and pull crawl space air into the system.
  • Air seal the floor. Seal gaps where pipes and wires pass through the subfloor to keep crawl space air out of living space.

Should a crawl space be vented or sealed?

Both approaches can work. Vented crawl spaces rely on outdoor air to carry moisture away, which works reasonably well in dry inland areas when the vents stay clear and the ground is covered. Sealed, or encapsulated, crawl spaces close off the vents, line the space with a heavy vapor barrier and control humidity mechanically. Sealing is a bigger project and has to be done to code, so it's worth a proper assessment before going that route.

What should you do if you find mold?

Don't scrape or spray it yourself without protection. Disturbing mold puts spores in the air. Start by finding and fixing the moisture source, since cleaning mold without fixing the cause just means it grows back. Then have affected materials cleaned or replaced, and replace any wet or moldy insulation.

After cleanup, check the crawl space again after the next good rain. If it stays dry, the fix worked. If moisture comes back, there's another source to track down.

faqs: Mold can trigger allergies and asthma symptoms and irritate the eyes, nose and throat, and air from a crawl space does make its way into the living space. Long-term moisture can also rot wood framing. It's worth addressing early, starting with the moisture source.
Will a dehumidifier stop crawl space mold?

A dehumidifier helps in a sealed, encapsulated crawl space. In a vented crawl space open to outdoor air, it's fighting the outdoors and won't do much. Fix drainage and add a vapor barrier first, then decide whether sealing and dehumidification make sense.
Can I use bleach on crawl space mold?

It's not a great choice. Bleach doesn't soak into porous wood well, adds harsh fumes in a tight space and doesn't fix the moisture problem. Address the moisture, then have affected materials properly cleaned or replaced.
How often should I check my crawl space?
Look at least once a year and after heavy rain. Check for standing water, damp insulation, leaks, musty smells and signs of pests.
